name: Bayern
summary_text: A gender-inclusive-language ban has been in force in all Bavarian public administration, schools and universities since 1 April 2024, following a Söder government declaration and cabinet decision. A visitor dealing with any registry office, police station, hospital admission desk or school operates in an environment where official gender-inclusive framing is prohibited — described in the dossier as "pure symbol politics" but practically a standing instruction of institutional hostility at every public counter. Bavaria is also a partner in the Sachsen/Thüringen/Sachsen-Anhalt Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act (SBGG). Bavarian police recorded 2,021 hate crimes in 2024 (up 8.2 % from 1,867 in 2023), but the LSBTIQ-specific breakdown was contested in a parliamentary query and the dossier cautions that high counts may reflect better police classification rather than greater danger. No documented street-violence incident specific to a trans visitor was found for Bavaria in this pass. National score is 0.71. Bayern sits 0.04 below: the legislative hostility (SBGG initiative) and the universal administrative-language ban create a uniformly colder official interface for a visitor, without the physical-attack evidence present in Brandenburg (0.66) or the equality-dismantling bill in Thüringen (0.65). The deviation reflects institutional posture rather than demonstrated violence.

sources.title: Ein Jahr Genderverbot in Bayern: Viel Lärm um sehr wenig? | tagesschau.de
sources.claim_summary: Tagesschau report on Bavaria's gender-language ban: from 1 April 2024, gender-inclusive German is prohibited in schools, universities and all state administration, implementing the Söder government declaration of December 2023 and a cabinet decision amending the language rules of public authorities; critics in the coverage dismiss it as symbol politics while noting its practical reach across every public counter, registry office and classroom.

sources.title: Länder wollen Gesetz zur Selbstbestimmung nachschärfen | ANTENNE BAYERN
sources.claim_summary: Antenne Bayern report on the Bundesrat initiative by several Länder — Sachsen, Thüringen and Sachsen-Anhalt, with Bavaria a partner — to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act (SBGG) on legal gender change, i.e. an organised Land-level attempt to make the nationwide self-ID law stricter.

sources.title: Herrmann stellt das Lagebild zur Hasskriminalität 2024 vor: StMI
sources.claim_summary: Bavarian Interior Ministry press release (Herrmann) presenting the 2024 hate-crime situation report for Bavaria: 2,021 recorded hate-crime offences, up 8.2 % on 2023's 1,867, published as the Land's own Lagebild; the dossier notes the LSBTIQ sub-category was contested in a parliamentary query and that Bavaria's comparatively high counts may reflect more thorough police classification rather than greater danger.
